problem: Microsoft wanted .NET to reach Linux and Mac developers and attract community contributions.
title: Microsoft open-sources .NET Core under the MIT license
context: The .NET framework was proprietary, with parts viewable under a restrictive licence.
decision_made: Release .NET Core, including the runtime and class libraries, as open source under the MIT licence with a patent covenant.
action_taken: Announced at the Connect() event and committed to working with the Mono community.
observed_outcome: Not documented in the sources used.
lessons: Opening code can serve a strategy of platform reach, though the scope of what is opened matters to the community.
limitations: Coverage disagrees on whether the entire framework or only a subset was opened. Later adoption was not checked.

claims.claim_text: Microsoft said .NET Core, including the runtime and framework libraries, would be open source under the MIT licence.
Coverage described the move as bringing .NET to Linux and Mac.
